chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abi 'Uyaynah, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a mouse that falls into a well, and he said: “If it comes out, then there is no harm; but if it has decomposed, then seven buckets [must be drawn].”

He said: And he was asked about a mouse that falls into the well, and no one knows of it until after one has performed wudu (ablution) from it. Should he repeat his wudu, his salat (prayer), and wash what it touched? He said: “No; the people of the house had already drawn from it and sprinkled [with it].”

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being ruled upon
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse, the source of impurity discussed in the ruling
key_terms.تَفَسَّخَتْ: decomposed or disintegrated in the water
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), whose repetition is being asked about
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), i.e., ritual washing for salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mouse falls into a well, and must wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer) be repeated if one did not know?
ai.summary: This hadith gives rulings concerning a mouse falling into a well and the effect on the water. It distinguishes between the case where the mouse is removed without decomposition and the case where it has decomposed, and it also states that prior wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer) are not to be repeated when the impurity was unknown at the time.
